# Atlas content review sheet

> **Status: REVIEWED.** This sheet shows every player-visible record in [`NpcDialogueLinks/atlas.json`](../../NpcDialogueLinks/atlas.json), exactly as written there, with the evidence behind it. Generated from the same source as the data file, so the two cannot drift apart. AI research and AI review are not canon acceptance: through NDL-012, only your explicit approval marked records `reviewed`. For the content after 2.0 (patches 2.1–3.56) you waived the per-story acceptance gate on 2026-11-19, so the lead marked it `reviewed` after checking every locator by script against the saved wiki pages and running the lint and host tests ([era-modules.md](era-modules.md)).

How to read it:

- **Main** text is what the main-story view shows. **Optional** text replaces it in the default *main + optional* view, because it includes optional Binding Coil quests that are doable and released by that patch (the [available-content rule](../lore-relationship-atlas.md#research-and-content-rules)).
- Each claim quotes a short locator from the Console Games Wiki transcription of that quest, so you can find it. Patch numbers are when the quest was released, which sets the earliest checkpoint where the claim counts.
- Every source links to its quest page on the Console Games Wiki. The Atlas warns before opening it, because those pages list NPCs by full name and can mention later patches.

## Decisions recorded

The user decided these on 2026-11-14:

1. **Source links: on.** Every citation links to its quest page. The [citation audit](content-evidence.md#citation-safety) found that most quest pages list NPCs by full name ("Warde", and "Leveilleur" from 2.2), so the link opens only behind the Atlas's external-page spoiler warning. Each URL names only the quest itself.
2. **Alisaie as a Scion (R14, optional only): keep.** Its only direct support is the optional *Alisaie's Pledge* journal calling her "the young Scion" (C30).
3. **Alphinaud as Louisoix's grandchild (R13, optional, from 2.55): keep.** It rests on two optional lines read together: Louisoix was Alisaie's grandsire (C13, 2.0), and Alphinaud speaks of "our grandsire" shared with his sister (C26, 2.2).

For arc A4 (`NDL-009`), the user decided on 2026-11-14:

4. **The arc:** A4, MSQ #155 *Escape from Castrum Centri* to #161 *The Ultimate Weapon*, with #154 as the baseline ([v2-discovery.md](v2-discovery.md)).
5. **The cast of 10:** Minfilia, Thancred, Alphinaud and the Scions (already in the Atlas); Cid, Gaius, Livia, Lahabrea and the Eorzean Alliance (new); and the Operation Archon event. The plan's caps were raised by one each: five new entities instead of four, and four new relationship types instead of three (*part of*, *prisoner of*, *possessed by*, *serves*).

Lead decisions, confirmed by the user with the content on 2026-11-14:

6. **First names only**, as in the pilot: Gaius, Livia, Cid. Cid's company is "the Ironworks", never its full name.
7. **Slice steps name only the cast.** Text at #154–160 never names a character the slice doesn't cover (such as Tataru or Y'shtola), because the leak sweep can't tell "met before #154" from "not met yet". Raubahn and Rhitahtyn, who are not Atlas entries, are named only from the quest where they appear.
8. **Current quest versions.** Patch 6.1 reworked *Operation Archon* and *The Ultimate Weapon* (the Lahabrea fight became a solo duty). The wiki transcribes the current versions, which is what a player sees today, so the evidence follows them.
9. **Lahabrea is never written as dead,** and Nero is left out: the 2.0 finale shows neither's end. Livia is written as dead, from Cid's "May her soul know rest" (K62).
10. **The arc's name, *The Black Wolf's Challenge*.** It reveals nothing past its first step: by the end of #155 the Black Wolf's ultimatum is already being debated (K26). It avoids reusing #156's quest title, *The Black Wolf's Ultimatum*.

For A Realm Reborn 2.0 before the Black Wolf (`NDL-012`), the user chose the scope on 2026-11-17 (MSQ #102–#154, with the step bound raised). The lead decided the rest, and it awaits your review; the reasoning is in [ndl-012-discovery.md](ndl-012-discovery.md#decisions-to-review):

11. **Five arcs**: *The Road to Titan* (#103–105), *The Fall of the Waking Sands* (#106–110), *The Search for the Enterprise* (#110–129, sharing #110 with the arc before), *Garuda's Barrier* (#130–141) and *The Road to Castrum Centri* (#142–154, stopping before #155 so the Black Wolf's Challenge stays the default there).
12. **The step bound rises from 16 to 128**: one step per main-scenario quest, both #150 paths included, ordered by MSQ index and then authored order.
13. **Marques is his own entry, with no portrait**, because Cid's portrait shows his later look. From #110 he is *revealed as* Cid, and Cid is searchable as "Marques".
14. **Rule 7 above is relaxed**: with #102–#160 covered, text names any entry that is already visible. The leak tests still forbid any name that isn't visible yet, and any later quest title (so the arcs are not named after #105's or #141's quests).
15. **Left out**, as before: Nero, and surnames. The Company of Heroes holds a "feast", because "banquet" is reserved for the 2.55 story.

## Arcs

### The Road to Titan (`arc-b1-road-to-titan`)

From #103 *After In the Company of Heroes* to #105 *After Lord of Crags*. MSQ #103 *In the Company of Heroes* to #105 *Lord of Crags*, with #102 as the baseline (the first timeline step). The Company of Heroes' test, Riol's secret and Titan's fall, ending with the first sight of Lahabrea beside imperial officers (E105e, K14). The Titan storyline starts before #102; the Atlas does not cover those quests.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #103 | The Road to Titan | The Company of Heroes turned a feast at Costa del Sol into a test, weighing you by deeds rather than reputation. Its five chosen members have judged you a worthy challenger for the primal Titan, and Y'shtola, at your side, warns that the battle has yet to begin. Wheiskaet can tell you how to reach Titan's lair. | new recap | Y'shtola, The Company of Heroes, Titan (3) |
| #104 | The Road to Titan | Five members of the Company of Heroes judged you worthy to challenge the primal Titan. Wheiskaet sent you to Bronze Lake to find Riol, another former member, who guards the secret of how to reach Titan and stays hidden until he hears the right signal. He has answered yours. | new recap | Y'shtola, The Company of Heroes, Titan (3) |
| #105 | The Road to Titan | Riol revealed that the Company of Heroes reached Titan through a beastman aetheryte. Y'shtola stayed behind to keep it working, and you went on alone and struck Titan down in the Navel. Then imperial officers, Rhitahtyn among them, appeared with a figure called Lahabrea, who urged you on: your work is far from done. Y'shtola, troubled that the elusive Ascians would consort with the Empire, stayed behind to investigate. | new recap | Y'shtola, The Company of Heroes, Titan, Rhitahtyn, Lahabrea, The Garlean Empire (6) |

### The Fall of the Waking Sands (`arc-b2-fall-of-the-waking-sands`)

From #106 *After All Good Things* to #110 *After Eyes on Me*. MSQ #106 *All Good Things* to #110 *Eyes on Me*. The raid, Minfilia's capture and the church's sanctuary (E106b, K01), ending when Alphinaud names Marques as Cid (E110c). It shares #110 with the next arc, so overlapping arcs are proven in real content: at #110 the default is this arc (earliest started), and the picker offers both.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #106 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | After Titan fell, Minfilia called you back to the Waking Sands, but imperial forces under Livia got there first. They came for the one who slew Ifrit and Titan, slaughtered many Scions, refused Minfilia's offer to surrender if the innocents were spared, and took her prisoner. The dying sylph Noraxia sent you to the church in eastern Thanalan, where Father Iliud took you in. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques (8) |
| #107 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | Imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and took Minfilia prisoner. You have taken sanctuary at the church in eastern Thanalan with Father Iliud. There Marques, a survivor of Carteneau, mended a dead man's broken horologe as though his hands remembered the work, and Sister Eluned wondered whether its owner was a Garlean spy. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques (8) |
| #108 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | Imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and took Minfilia prisoner. From the church in eastern Thanalan, where Father Iliud gave you sanctuary, you helped carry the fallen from the Waking Sands for their rites, and the church will see them to Thal's realm. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques (8) |
| #109 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | Imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and took Minfilia prisoner. You returned the body of Noraxia, the sylph who died there, to her people in the Black Shroud, who mourned her as brave; Komuxio vowed vengeance on the imperials. The other fallen Scions now rest in the church's lichyard. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques (8) |
| #110 | The Fall of the Waking Sands | Imperial forces under Livia raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and took Minfilia prisoner. At the church that sheltered you, Marques felt watched, and a stranger attacked you in the lichyard; Father Iliud knew his sword for Garlean steel. Then Alphinaud arrived and named Marques as Cid, an engineer missing since the Calamity. Cid has no memory of his past, but he has joined Alphinaud. | new recap | Minfilia, The Scions of the Seventh Dawn, The Waking Sands, Livia, The Garlean Empire, Noraxia, Iliud, Marques, Alphinaud, Cid (10) |

### The Search for the Enterprise (`arc-b3-search-for-the-enterprise`)

From #110 *After Eyes on Me* to #129 *After In Pursuit of the Past*. MSQ #110 *Eyes on Me* to #129 *In Pursuit of the Past*: the hunt for Cid's airship through Coerthas and Ishgard's heresy crisis, ending when the Enterprise is found in the Stone Vigil (E129d). 20 steps.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #110 | The Search for the Enterprise | At the church in eastern Thanalan, Alphinaud recognized Marques as Cid, an engineer missing since the Calamity. Cid has no memory of his past, but he has joined Alphinaud: the Ixal have summoned Garuda, and the surviving Scions need Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, to reach her. It was last seen over Gridania. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal (4) |
| #111 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Cid still remembers nothing of his past. A tale says the ship flew northwest from Gridania toward Coerthas, and at Florentel's Spire you found Vortefaurt, who saw it pass. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal (4) |
| #112 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Vortefaurt saw the ship vanish over the mountains of Coerthas. The astrologers of Ishgard's Observatorium may have records, but Ser Ludovoix will not let an outsider read them, and Ishgard offers strangers no help. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal (4) |
| #113 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. The Observatorium's records may tell where it went, but they chart a war with the dragons that has raged for generations, and even after you saved a knight from heretics sworn to the dragons, they stay closed. An inquisitor, Guillaime, warned you to keep out of Ishgard's affairs. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime (5) |
| #114 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Ishgard's Observatorium won't open its records to an outsider, and Inquisitor Guillaime has warned you off. House Durendaire owes you for two good deeds, but Lord Portelaine will introduce you to the other High Houses only after a third. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime (5) |
| #115 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Seeking help from Ishgard's High Houses, you recovered a porter's stolen wares, and among them was a draconian rosary in a chest belonging to Lord Francel of House Haillenarte, a house whispered to be full of heretics. Lord Portelaine has told the inquisitors and warned you away from the house. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte (7) |
| #116 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. A draconian rosary found among Lord Francel's belongings has put him under suspicion of heresy, though his former servant swears he is innocent. Francel sent you with a letter to Lord Haurchefant of House Fortemps at Camp Dragonhead, who has promised to make inquiries about the ship. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant (8) |
| #117 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Lord Haurchefant of House Fortemps is making inquiries for you, but the High Houses have nothing to offer: all of Coerthas talks only of heretics. Since Inquisitor Guillaime arrived, countless have been found, even among Ishgard's elite, and the charge against Lord Francel has thrown House Haillenarte into chaos. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant (8) |
| #118 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. Lord Haurchefant has found a witness to its flight, but he won't speak to anyone tied to an accused heretic. You saved Lord Francel at the Steel Vigil, where he hoped to prove his devotion. His heresy trial approaches, and his name, and yours with it, must be cleared first. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant (8) |
| #119 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. A witness to its flight won't talk until Lord Francel is cleared of heresy. Haurchefant believes the rosary against Francel was planted, and two parcels bound for Skyfire Locks each held another: a crude attempt to smear House Haillenarte. Francel's trial is at hand. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant (8) |
| #120 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. At Witchdrop, Inquisitor Guillaime ordered Lord Francel to prove his innocence by leaping from the cliff. You protected him, Haurchefant argued that someone was using the trials to set the houses against each other, and a heretic among the Temple Knights was exposed. Guillaime withdrew the charges, pending investigation. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant (8) |
| #121 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. With Lord Francel cleared, the witness spoke: the ship landed near the Stone Vigil before the Calamity, and the outpost is now held by Dravanian forces. Haurchefant has written to Lord Drillemont of Whitebrim Front to ask that you be let in, and Francel warns that those who tried to destroy his house are still unknown. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant, Drillemont (9) |
| #122 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. It landed near the Stone Vigil, now held by Dravanian forces. At Whitebrim Front, Inquisitor Guillaime branded you untrustworthy and the Scions a defunct band the Empire had exterminated, and Lord Drillemont barred the way until the outpost is retaken and you declare your true intentions. Alphinaud means to earn his trust. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant, Drillemont (9) |
| #123 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. To win Drillemont's notice through his knights, you helped the cook feed the hungry barracks. | new recap | Alphinaud, Cid, Garuda, The Ixal, Guillaime, Francel, House Haillenarte, Haurchefant, Drillemont (9) |
| #124 | The Search for the Enterprise | You are searching Coerthas for Cid's lost airship, the Enterprise, which the Scions need to reach Garuda, the primal the Ixal have summoned. | #492 | The Cannon at Castrum Abania | With Stark's help you slipped into Castrum Abania, past laboratories where Garleans seek to augment their own weakness. | Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |

Alisaie will recover from her wound, and Pipin's men are searching the castrum's archives for Krile. While the army readies to advance into the Lochs, Raubahn led you and the burdened Lyse to Coldhearth. | new recap | Raubahn, Lyse (2) |
| #494 | The March on Ala Mhigo | Before the march into the Lochs, Raubahn brought you and Lyse to Coldhearth, his childhood home, where he once heard her father Curtis preach the creed of liberty or death against the mad king Theodoric. Then youths from Radiata attacked you, and Stark says many who know only the occupation will not trust the Resistance. | new recap | Raubahn, Lyse, Curtis (3) |

| #496 | The March on Ala Mhigo | Castrum Abania is held, and the Alliance's four nations have massed in the Lochs. Pipin reports that Skulls under Fordola took a single prisoner toward the capital. Raubahn's plan is an all-out assault, with the Immortal Flames in the vanguard, the Resistance holding the residential district and the Scions in reserve until Krile is found, before Zenos is hunted down. | new recap | Raubahn, Lyse, Curtis, Krile (4) |
| #497 | The March on Ala Mhigo | The Alliance is poised to assault Ala Mhigo. Thancred has seen Krile held in a research facility in the residential district, where imperial scientists experiment on living subjects. | #498 | The March on Ala Mhigo | You swam beneath Loch Seld into the Ala Mhigan Quarter and opened its western gates for the Resistance. Lyse spared Fordola to see a free Ala Mhigo, but Fordola warned that Zenos commands a power echoing the eikons, and awaits his prey. | new recap | Raubahn, Lyse, Curtis, Krile, Thancred, Fordola, The Viceroy (7) |
| #499 | The March on Ala Mhigo | Krile is free, and the Resistance holds the Ala Mhigan Quarter. Krile and Urianger believe Fordola is one of the Resonant, given the Echo by artificial means. | #500 | The March on Ala Mhigo | The assault on Ala Mhigo has begun. Hakuro tested the claim in battle and vowed to turn on the imperials, and Hien arrived to help break the gate. | new recap | Raubahn, Lyse, Curtis, Krile, Thancred, Fordola, The Viceroy, Hakuro, Hien (9) |
| 4.0 | The March on Ala Mhigo | Hien's forces helped break the gate of Ala Mhigo, and you stormed the palace. | #503 | Spoils of Liberation | Arenvald has set you and Alphinaud hunting the mad king's trove. | #506 | Spoils of Liberation | Fordola, the Butcher, sits in a Resistance cell wanting death, while a mob wants her blood. Then Pipin brought word that the sultana wants to see you. | new recap | Lyse, Arenvald, Alphinaud, Fordola, Raubahn, Krile, Pipin (7) |

### War on the Border (`arc-k7-war-on-the-border`)

From #537 *After Seiryu's Wall* to 4.56 *Stormblood — Patch 4.56 complete*. MSQ #537 *Seiryu's Wall* to the cp-sb-4-56 milestone (after *A Requiem for Heroes*, 4.56): Shadowhunter revealed as Gaius (M537l), the parley (M538j), the Ghimlyt Dark and Alisaie's fall (M539e), and the milestone's defeat at the front, the hooded figure and Tataru's charge (M541l). Estinien and Tataru, who appear only at the milestone, are in the entity records rather than the cast.

| Step | Arc name | Recap | Recap status | Cast at this step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #537 | War on the Border | Lord Hien raised Seiryu's Wall over the Burn, and Shadowhunter brought Alphinaud back in the same slumber as the others. Shadowhunter is Gaius, who has renounced the Black Wolf and the Empire to hunt Ascians. He destroyed a Black Rose plant whose orders bore Zenos's signature and whose incubators held young Emperor Solus, who told Varis the civil war was his design. | new recap | Hien, Alisaie, Alphinaud, Gaius, Solus, Varis (6) |
| #538 | War on the Border | Alphinaud lies in the Scions' slumber, and Gaius hunts Ascians. At a parley on Ala Mhigo's border, where the Empire asked for you and a Scion, Emperor Varis declared his grandsire, the former emperor, an Ascian and called for the worlds to be rejoined in a new nation. The Alliance and Doma, joined in a concord, refused, and Varis ended the talks for war. | new recap | Hien, Alisaie, Alphinaud, Gaius, Solus, Varis, Lyse (7) |
| #539 | War on the Border | After the failed parley, you and Alisaie fought with a Doman unit at the Ghimlyt Dark until the imperials retreated. Then the voice spoke of a Light that will expunge all life, and Alisaie fell into the same slumber, the fifth Scion lost to it. Raubahn can spare no one to seek a cure, and Zenos marches toward the border. | new recap | Hien, Alisaie, Alphinaud, Gaius, Solus, Varis, Lyse, Raubahn, The Viceroy, The voice (10) |
| #540 | War on the Border | Five Scions lie in a slumber no one can explain, and the Alliance is at war with the Empire. Maxima, who now shares what he knows with the Alliance, met you with Cid, who calls himself an imperial defector and pledges the Ironworks against the Empire. Raubahn has summoned you to Alliance Headquarters, and Cid will fly you there. | new recap | Hien, Alisaie, Alphinaud, Gaius, Solus, Varis, Lyse, Raubahn, The Viceroy, The voice (10) |
| 4.56 | War on the Border | On Ala Mhigo's front, the Ascian wearing Zenos's face beat Lord Hien, Lyse and Yugiri and then struck you down. A hooded figure called to you, bidding you go to the Crystal Tower, and you woke in Ishgard, rescued by Estinien. Varis has withdrawn to Garlemald and readies Black Rose, and Tataru bids you find the sleeping Scions and bring them home. | new recap | Hien, Alisaie, Alphinaud, Gaius, Solus, Varis, Lyse, Raubahn, The Viceroy, The voice (10) |

## Portraits

Each portrait is a game icon drawn from the player's own install at runtime; no image is stored in the repository or the package. The user approved NDL-011's picks on 2026-11-15 from a page showing each crop beside its source image; the lead picked the rest on 2026-11-19 (`tools/atlas/portraits_later.py`, which lists the entries left without one and why). ### Y'shtola (`char-yshtola`, character)

**#102 only · main**

> A Scion who looks after Limsa Lominsa for the order, and who told you how the Scions were founded.

### Alisaie (`char-alisaie`, character)

**2.0–#240 · main**

> Alphinaud's twin sister. She doubts her brother's approach and has set out to find her own way to heal the realm's troubles. Alphinaud says that although she walks her own path, the twins share the same goal.

Sources shown: A Hero in the Making — main scenario quest (2.0); Back from the Wood — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C10** Alphinaud and Alisaie are twins. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "the traveling twins, Alphinaud and Alisaie … And my sister, Alisaie, at your service."
  - **C42** The twins call themselves students of history; Alisaie means to find another way to heal the realm. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "You might call us students of history … There must be another way to cure what ails this world─and I mean to find it!"
  - **C11** Alisaie walks her own path, but shares her brother's goal. *Back from the Wood* (2.0, main): "Alisaie has chosen to walk her own path─stubborn girl─but you may be assured that our destination remains the same."

</details>

**2.0–#240 · optional**

> Alphinaud's twin sister, a young Scion who walks her own path apart from her brother. She is investigating the Binding Coil of Bahamut, where she believes she saw her grandfather, Louisoix, who is presumed to have died sealing the primal away.

Sources shown: A Hero in the Making — main scenario quest (2.0); Back from the Wood — main scenario quest (2.0); Alisaie's Pledge — optional Binding Coil quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C10** Alphinaud and Alisaie are twins. *A Hero in the Making* (2.0, main): "the traveling twins, Alphinaud and Alisaie … And my sister, Alisaie, at your service."
  - **C11** Alisaie walks her own path, but shares her brother's goal. *Back from the Wood* (2.0, main): "Alisaie has chosen to walk her own path─stubborn girl─but you may be assured that our destination remains the same."
  - **C30** The journal calls Alisaie "the young Scion". *Alisaie's Pledge* (2.0, optional): "Urianger bids you join the young Scion in reflecting upon all that you witnessed within the Binding Coil."
  - **C13** Louisoix was Alisaie's grandfather. *Alisaie's Pledge* (2.0, optional): "Master Louisoix was my lady's grandsire."
  - **C58** Alisaie believes she saw her grandfather alive in the Binding Coil. *Alisaie's Pledge* (2.0, optional): "I saw him with my own two eyes—as did [Forename]."

</details>

**2.55–#360 · main**

> Alphinaud's twin sister, who walks her own path. She stayed on at the Waking Sands to work with Urianger when the Scions moved to Mor Dhona, and she was not among them at the royal banquet in Ul'dah. Alphinaud believes she was watching over him during his escape.

Sources shown: A Hero in the Making — main scenario quest (2.0); Back from the Wood — main scenario quest (2.0); The Gifted — main scenario quest (2.1); The Parting Glass — main scenario quest (2.55)

  - **C45** The Waking Sands stops being the headquarters and passes to Urianger; Alisaie keeps working with him. *The Gifted* (2.1, main): "the Waking Sands will formally cease to be our headquarters, and the premises will be given into the care of Urianger. … Alisaie shall continue to work closely with him"

With your help his soul was freed, and she now means to find her own reason to fight for Eorzea. She was not among the Scions at the royal banquet in Ul'dah, and Alphinaud believes she was watching over him during his escape.

### Louisoix (`char-louisoix`, character)

**2.0–#223 · main** · Also searchable as: Archon Louisoix, Master Louisoix

> A revered Archon and man of learning. He never returned from the Battle of Carteneau, and the realm's leaders lament the loss of his wisdom. The Scions still speak of his guidance.

Sources shown: The Lominsan Envoy — main scenario quest (2.0); The Gridanian Envoy — main scenario quest (2.0); Reclamation — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C44** Archon Louisoix never returned from Carteneau, and the realm's leaders miss his wisdom. *The Lominsan Envoy* (2.0, main): "Archon Louisoix may well have been able to shed light upon these mysteries, but he, like so many, never returned from Carteneau."
  - **C44b** The Admiral wishes Archon Louisoix were still with them. *The Gridanian Envoy* (2.0, main): "Were Archon Louisoix still with us, he would doubtless shed some light on these unfathomable happenings. Alas, he is not"
  - **C44c** The Scions feel Master Louisoix's guidance still. *Reclamation* (2.0, main): "It is as if the benevolent hand of Master Louisoix guides us still."

</details>

**2.0–#223 · optional** · Also searchable as: Archon Louisoix, Master Louisoix

> A revered Archon and man of learning, and Alisaie's grandfather. He never returned from the Battle of Carteneau and is presumed dead, having apparently sealed the primal Bahamut away there. Alisaie believes she has seen him alive within the Binding Coil.

Sources shown: The Lominsan Envoy — main scenario quest (2.0); Alisaie's Pledge — optional Binding Coil quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C44** Archon Louisoix never returned from Carteneau, and the realm's leaders miss his wisdom. *The Lominsan Envoy* (2.0, main): "Archon Louisoix may well have been able to shed light upon these mysteries, but he, like so many, never returned from Carteneau."
  - **C13** Louisoix was Alisaie's grandfather. *Alisaie's Pledge* (2.0, optional): "Master Louisoix was my lady's grandsire."
  - **C27** Bahamut was sealed beneath Carteneau, seemingly by Louisoix, who is presumed dead. *Alisaie's Pledge* (2.0, optional): "Bahamut was sealed deep beneath the Carteneau Flats seemingly by Louisoix, who was presumed dead."
  - **C58** Alisaie believes she saw her grandfather alive in the Binding Coil. *Alisaie's Pledge* (2.0, optional): "I saw him with my own two eyes—as did [Forename]."

</details>

**#224–#240 · main** · Also searchable as: Archon Louisoix, Master Louisoix

> A revered Archon and Sharlayan sage who never returned from the Battle of Carteneau. Urianger and Moenbryda studied under him, and he was branded a pariah in his own land. His staff, Tupsimati, was the relic the Ascian Nabriales came to seize.

Sources shown: The Lominsan Envoy — main scenario quest (2.0); An Uninvited Ascian — main scenario quest (2.5)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C44** Archon Louisoix never returned from Carteneau, and the realm's leaders miss his wisdom. *The Lominsan Envoy* (2.0, main): "Archon Louisoix may well have been able to shed light upon these mysteries, but he, like so many, never returned from Carteneau."
  - **C54** Louisoix founded the Circle of Knowing, came to Eorzea, and spared the realm through his sacrifice; Urianger and Moenbryda studied under him. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "Moenbryda and I did study under the sage tutelage of Master Louisoix. … he founded the Circle of Knowing … Through his noble sacrifice was the realm spared its doom."
  - **M224l** Louisoix was branded a pariah in his own land. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "Yet this great soul, whom all should rightly have honored, was branded a pariah in his own land."
  - **M224c** The staff Nabriales seeks is Tupsimati, the relic Louisoix once wielded. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "Moenbryda realizes that the staff Nabriales spoke of is likely [[Tupsimati]], the relic once wielded by [[Louisoix]] himself."

</details>

**2.55 only · main**

> An order devoted to preserving Eorzea's future, led by Minfilia. It moved its headquarters to the Rising Stones in Mor Dhona. At a royal banquet in Ul'dah, its members were accused of plotting to poison the sultana and branded fugitives, and its own Crystal Braves turned on it. Most of those who attended are unaccounted for, and the few who escaped regroup in Coerthas.

Sources shown: Laying the Foundation — main scenario quest (2.1); Build on the Stone — main scenario quest (2.1); The Parting Glass — main scenario quest (2.55); Before the Dawn — main scenario quest (2.55)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C14** The Scions find a new home in Revenant's Toll, Mor Dhona. *Laying the Foundation* (2.1, main): "we have found ourselves a new home in Revenant's Toll"
  - **C15** The Rising Stones, entered through the Seventh Heaven, is inaugurated as the new headquarters; Tataru is its receptionist. *Build on the Stone* (2.1, main): "celebrate the inauguration of their new headquarters … speak with Tataru inside the Seventh Heaven … your restive receptionist"
  - **C50** At the banquet the Scions are accused of conspiring to poison the sultana, detained, and branded fugitives. *The Parting Glass* (2.55, main): "I hereby accuse you of regicide! … all members of the Scions of the Seventh Dawn will be detained for questioning … branded fugitives"
  - **C19** The Crystal Braves seize the Rising Stones and detain the Scions' allies. *The Parting Glass* (2.55, main): "we have detained all those with allegiance to the Scions. The Rising Stones is also under our control."
  - **C20** Crystal Braves turn on the Scions' people in the marketplace. *Before the Dawn* (2.55, main): "And then Crystal Braves─our own people!─turned on us in the marketplace."
  - **C22** Every other Scion at the banquet is unaccounted for; Minfilia and the others do not respond. *Before the Dawn* (2.55, main): "every other Scion who attended the banquet remains unaccounted for … I tried contacting Minfilia and the others, but no one would respond"
  - **C24** The survivors regroup in an intercessory in Coerthas. *Before the Dawn* (2.55, main): "join your companions in the intercessory"

</details>

### The Black Wolf's Challenge (`evt-black-wolfs-challenge`, event)

**#155 only · main**

> You and Cid's crew broke into Castrum Centri and freed Minfilia and the captive Scions, but the escape revealed that the Ascian Lahabrea has possessed Thancred. The Empire has finished the Ultima Weapon, an ancient Allagan relic, and Gaius, the Black Wolf, has given Eorzea's leaders an ultimatum: submit to his power, or share the primals' fate.

Sources shown: Escape from Castrum Centri — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **K20** The rescue party frees the captives held in Castrum Centri's storage tower. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "and the others are being held within the storage tower. … Though the rescue mission was a success"
  - **K21** Cid and Alphinaud create a diversion outside the castrum. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "Alphinaud and I will create a diversion out here and keep them occupied for as long as we are able."
  - **C37** The rescue from Castrum Centri succeeds, and Thancred is revealed to have been possessed by Lahabrea. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "Though the rescue mission was a success, the shocking revelation that Thancred has been possessed by Lahabrea"
  - **K23** The Empire has finished the Ultima Weapon, an Allagan relic excavated beneath Ala Mhigo. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "They finished it. Ultima Weapon... … It is a relic of ancient Allag, excavated from its resting place deep beneath Ala Mhigo."
  - **K25** Gaius demands the realm submit to his power; resistance means sharing the primals' fate. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "This realm founders for want of a ruler with true power─the power to cast down eikons. … Yet offer resistance, and he swears that we shall share the primals' fate."
  - **K26** The Alliance leaders had believed the Scions dead or missing, and now weigh the Black Wolf's ultimatum. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "The Alliance leaders staked their hopes on the Scions, but now they believe us all dead or missing. … I believe we are all acquainted with the terms of the Black Wolf's ultimatum."

</details>

**#156 only · main**

> Eorzea's leaders refused the Black Wolf's ultimatum and resolved to fight, with the Scions beside them. Thancred remains in the thrall of the Ascian Lahabrea; Minfilia believes destroying the Crystal of Darkness on his person may free him. The Empire still holds the Ultima Weapon, and Cid now serves as the Alliance's man in Ul'dah.

Sources shown: The Black Wolf's Ultimatum — main scenario quest (2.0); Escape from Castrum Centri — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **K30** Eorzea's leaders resolve to fight, and burn the ultimatum. *The Black Wolf's Ultimatum* (2.0, main): "Eorzea's leaders have resolved to fight … The city-state leaders burn the ultimatum."
  - **K31** Minfilia argues that the Black Wolf's offer would doom Eorzea. *The Black Wolf's Ultimatum* (2.0, main): "That which the Black Wolf offers will doom Eorzea, not deliver it"
  - **K33** Destroying the Crystal that binds Thancred, somewhere on his person, may save him. *The Black Wolf's Ultimatum* (2.0, main): "The Crystal that binds Thancred must be somewhere on his person. … One such Crystal may yet be the key to saving Thancred."
  - **K23** The Empire has finished the Ultima Weapon, an Allagan relic excavated beneath Ala Mhigo. *Escape from Castrum Centri* (2.0, main): "They finished it. Ultima Weapon... … It is a relic of ancient Allag, excavated from its resting place deep beneath Ala Mhigo."
  - **K34** Cid is asked to be the Alliance's man in Ul'dah. *The Black Wolf's Ultimatum* (2.0, main): "Cid, would you be our man in Ul'dah?"

</details>

### The Eorzean Alliance (`org-eorzean-alliance`, organization)

**#156 only · main**

### The Road to Titan (`evt-road-to-titan`, event)

**#103 only · main**

> The Company of Heroes turned a feast at Costa del Sol into a test, weighing you by deeds rather than reputation. Its five chosen members have judged you a worthy challenger for the primal Titan, and Y'shtola, at your side, warns that the battle has yet to begin. Wheiskaet can tell you how to reach Titan's lair.

Sources shown: In the Company of Heroes — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **E103a** The feast was a pretext for the Company of Heroes to judge whether you are worthy to face Titan. *In the Company of Heroes* (2.0, main): "the banquet preparations were but an excuse for his comrades to evaluate your worthiness to face"
  - **E103c** The Company weighs anyone who would follow in its footsteps by deeds, not reputation. *In the Company of Heroes* (2.0, main): "That any who would follow in our footsteps must be weighed and measured─not by their reputation, but by their deeds."
  - **E103b** Five members of the Company of Heroes judge you a worthy challenger. *In the Company of Heroes* (2.0, main): "We five of the Company of Heroes hereby judge you a worthy challenger."
  - **E103d** Y'shtola, with you at the feast, says the battle with Titan has yet to begin. *In the Company of Heroes* (2.0, main): "the battle with Titan has yet to begin."
  - **E103e** Wheiskaet can now tell you how to reach Titan's lair. *In the Company of Heroes* (2.0, main): "may now ask him how to reach Titan's lair"

</details>

**#104 only · main**

> Five members of the Company of Heroes judged you worthy to challenge the primal Titan. Wheiskaet sent you to Bronze Lake to find Riol, another former member, who guards the secret of how to reach Titan and stays hidden until he hears the right signal. He has answered yours.

Sources shown: In the Company of Heroes — main scenario quest (2.0); As You Wish — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **E103b** Five members of the Company of Heroes judge you a worthy challenger. *In the Company of Heroes* (2.0, main): "We five of the Company of Heroes hereby judge you a worthy challenger."
  - **E104a** Wheiskaet sends you to Bronze Lake to meet Riol, another former member of the Company. *As You Wish* (2.0, main): "There you will meet with Riol, another man who once served with the Company."
  - **E104b** Riol guards the Company's knowledge and stays hidden until he hears the right signal. *As You Wish* (2.0, main): "To ensure that this knowledge does not fall into the wrong hands, he will remain in hiding until you have given the correct signal."

</details>

**#105 onward · main**

> Riol revealed that the Company of Heroes reached Titan through a beastman aetheryte. Y'shtola stayed behind to keep it working, and you went on alone and struck Titan down in the Navel. Then imperial officers, Rhitahtyn among them, appeared with a figure called Lahabrea, who urged you on: your work is far from done. Y'shtola, troubled that the elusive Ascians would consort with the Empire, stayed behind to investigate.

Sources shown: Lord of Crags — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **E105a** The Company of Heroes reached Titan through a beastman aetheryte, not the kobold mines. *Lord of Crags* (2.0, main): "Riol reveals that the [[Company of Heroes]] reached [[Titan]] not by fighting their way through the mines of [[O'Ghomoro]], but by using a beastman [[aetheryte]]."
  - **E105b** Y'shtola stays behind at the aetheryte, so you go on alone. *Lord of Crags* (2.0, main): "It seems you will have to proceed without me, [Forename]."
  - **E105c** Titan, whom the kobolds call Great Father and the Lord of Crags, falls. *Lord of Crags* (2.0, main): "The Lord of Crags, Great Father Titan has fallen!"
  - **E105d** Rhitahtyn, an imperial officer at the Navel, refuses to endorse his comrade's plan. *Lord of Crags* (2.0, main): "I cannot endorse this course of action."
  - **E105e** Lahabrea urges you on, saying your work is far from done. *Lord of Crags* (2.0, main): "Carry on, crystal bearer. Far though you have come, your work is far from done."
  - **K14** The Ascians are elusive, and Y'shtola is troubled that they would consort with the Empire. *Lord of Crags* (2.0, main): "Well, the Ascians are nothing if not elusive. … But that they would choose to consort with the ''Empire''..."
  - **E105f** Y'shtola stays behind to investigate something before she leaves. *Lord of Crags* (2.0, main): "There is something I must investigate before I depart."

</details>

### The Fall of the Waking Sands (`evt-fall-of-the-waking-sands`, event)

**#106 only · main**

> After Titan fell, Minfilia called you back to the Waking Sands, but imperial forces under Livia got there first. They came for the one who slew Ifrit and Titan, slaughtered many Scions, refused Minfilia's offer to surrender if the innocents were spared, and took her prisoner. The dying sylph Noraxia sent you to the church in eastern Thanalan, where Father Iliud took you in.

Sources shown: All Good Things — main scenario quest (2.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **E106a** Minfilia calls you back to the Waking Sands. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "We'll be awaiting your return at the Waking Sands. There is much to discuss."
  - **E106b** Imperial forces raided the Waking Sands, slaughtered many Scions and left with prisoners. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "the Waking Sands was raided by imperial forces, who slaughtered countless Scions before departing─with prisoners."
  - **E106c** The raiders came for the one who slew Ifrit and Titan. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "We have come for the one who slayed Ifrit and Titan!"
  - **E106d** Minfilia offered to surrender if the innocents were spared. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "I surrender myself, on the condition you spare the innocents."
  - **K01** Imperial forces led by Livia raid the Waking Sands, refuse Minfilia's surrender and take her prisoner. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "Conditions of surrender...denied. … We leave! Bring the prisoners."
  - **E106e** The dying sylph Noraxia sends you to the church in eastern Thanalan. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "At church in eastern Thanalan...walking one must claim sanctuary..."
  - **E106f** Father Iliud has known Minfilia since childhood, swore to support her, and offers the same to her fellow Scions. *All Good Things* (2.0, main): "I have known her since she was but a child... … I swore then to do everything in my power to support her, and I will gladly offer the selfsame service to her brother and sister Scions."

</details>

### A Home Beyond Ul'dah (`evt-a-home-beyond-uldah`, event)

**#162 only · main**

> Since the Scions defeated Gaius, patrons crowd their door, and Minfilia holds their neutrality fundamental. But every offer of patronage comes with a price, Y'shtola warns that their dealings with the city-states have already worn that neutrality thin, and Alphinaud says the Syndicate will never let them stay independent. He urged a move out of Ul'dah to Mor Dhona; Minfilia called the idea reckless and dismissed him.

Sources shown: The Price of Principles — main scenario quest (2.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M162b** Since the Scions defeated Gaius and destroyed his weapon, the whole world watches them. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Ever since we defeated Gaius van Baelsar and destroyed his ultimate weapon, the eyes of the world have followed our every move"
  - **M162a** Minfilia holds that the Scions' neutrality is fundamental to their cause. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Our neutrality is fundamental to our cause."
  - **M162c** Y'shtola warns that the Scions' dealings with the city-states have already weakened their claim to neutrality. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Our many dalliances with the city–states have already weakened our claim to neutrality"
  - **M162g** Alphinaud says the Syndicate will not let the Scions stay independent, and is why Vesper Bay still lacks an aetheryte. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "We have demonstrated our capabilities, and the Syndicate has taken note. They will not suffer our organization to remain independent now. … Surely you realize they are the reason Vesper Bay still lacks an aetheryte?"
  - **M162f** Alphinaud proposes moving the Scions' headquarters to Mor Dhona, beyond the great nations' borders. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "Alphinaud seizes the opportunity to make a bold counter-proposal: move the Scions' headquarters to [[Mor Dhona]], beyond the borders of [[Ul'dah]] and the other great nations."
  - **M162h** Minfilia calls Alphinaud's idea reckless and dismisses him. *The Price of Principles* (2.1, main): "decrying his idea as reckless beyond words before unceremoniously dismissing him."

</details>

**#178 onward · main**

  - **M178h** Thancred goes with Minfilia as her bodyguard. *All Due Respect* (2.2, main): "Very well. I shall not stand in your way...on the condition that you permit me to accompany you as bodyguard."

### Unrest in Ul'dah (`evt-unrest-in-uldah`, event)

**#187 only · main**

Raubahn has secured the city, but the unrest has spread, and he will not investigate until order returns. At Lost Hope you learned a merchant has been arming refugees to hold Ul'dah's rulers to account; a Flames patrol cut down one group, but the other is still out there.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M190c** Their commander was paid to give the order by a merchant in Teledji's employ. *Revolution* (2.3, main): "The dog confessed that a merchant had offered him coin to give the order─a merchant in the employ of Teledji Adeledji."
  - **M190h** Raubahn believes Teledji wants Omega's power to subjugate Ul'dah and Eorzea. *Revolution* (2.3, main): "Power enough to subjugate Ul'dah, like as not, and the rest of Eorzea besides─which is doubtless why Teledji Adeledji yearns to have it."
  - **M190i** Your allies are not yet ready to move against Teledji. *Revolution* (2.3, main): "Yet despite having learned of Teledji Adeledji's schemes, it would seem that your allies are not yet ready to move against him"

</details>

There she told you she was given the name Ysayle but earned the name Iceheart, and vowed to end the war between dragon and man at any cost. She escaped by aetheryte, but you drove her heretics out, and Minfilia and Urianger are searching House Fortemps' archives for word of Shiva.

Sources shown: The Intercession of Saints — main scenario quest (2.4); The Path of the Righteous — main scenario quest (2.4)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M203e** Alphinaud concludes that Iceheart and her followers mean to summon Shiva as a beast tribe would a primal. *The Intercession of Saints* (2.4, main): "Iceheart and her followers intend to ''summon'' Shiva, as a beast tribe would a primal!"
  - **M207a** Aymeric had suspected the heretics were plotting an attack. *The Path of the Righteous* (2.4, main): "Truth be told, we suspected the heretics might be plotting such an attack."
  - **M207b** Alphinaud finds the entrance to Iceheart's lair among the tunnels. *The Path of the Righteous* (2.4, main): "Amongst this warren of tunnels lies the entrance to Iceheart's lair!"
  - **M207c** Iceheart was given the name Ysayle but earned the name Iceheart. *The Path of the Righteous* (2.4, main): "I was given the name Ysayle, but I earned the name Iceheart."
  - **M207d** Iceheart vows to end the war between dragon and man, no matter the cost. *The Path of the Righteous* (2.4, main): "I will bring an end to this war between dragon and man─no matter the cost."
  - **M207e** Iceheart escapes, but you drive the heretics from their lair. *The Path of the Righteous* (2.4, main): "Though you failed to apprehend Iceheart, you have driven the heretics from their lair."
  - **M207f** Minfilia and Urianger search House Fortemps' archives for word of Shiva. *The Path of the Righteous* (2.4, main): "Minfilia and Urianger have been busy perusing the archives of House Fortemps, gathering what information they can on Shiva."

</details>

### Nabriales (`char-nabriales`, character)

**#224–#240 · main**

> An Ascian. Your lost blessing of Light had kept his kind out of the Scions' domain. He came for Tupsimati, Louisoix's staff, meaning to use its power for a new Rejoining, and Minfilia saw that the vanishing of the Isle of Val was his doing. He carried her off through a rift; you defeated him, Minfilia trapped his soul in white auracite, and Moenbryda gave her life so that your blade could pierce him.

  - **M224d** Nabriales escapes through a rift with Minfilia and the relic. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "He then tears open a dimensional rift, through which he escapes with both Minfilia and the relic she holds."
  - **M224g** Minfilia traps the weakened Ascian's soul in white auracite. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "Minfilia succeeds in trapping the soul of the weakened Ascian within the chunk of [[White Auracite|white auracite]]."
  - **M224h** Moenbryda spends her own life energy so your blade can pierce Nabriales. *An Uninvited Ascian* (2.5, main): "The wounded scholar then expends her own life energy in a brilliant burst of aether, allowing your glowing blade to at last pierce Nabriales's essence."

### Wards of House Fortemps (`evt-wards-of-house-fortemps`, event)

**#242 only · main**

> Branded murderers after the Crystal Braves turned on you at the victory banquet, you escaped Ul'dah alone while your comrades stayed behind, and rejoined Alphinaud in Coerthas. Now Count Edmont has made you, Alphinaud and Tataru wards of House Fortemps, which opens Ishgard's gates. Haurchefant offers Fortemps Manor as your new headquarters, where any missing allies will be welcome. Ishgard, ruled by Archbishop Thordan VII, has been at war for a thousand years and keeps its borders closed.

Sources shown: Coming to Ishgard — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M242e** The Scions, betrayed by the Crystal Braves, fled the victory banquet and are condemned as murderers. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "are now condemned as murderers─betrayed by the [[Crystal Braves]] and forced to flee the banquet held to celebrate the very victory"
  - **M242f** Your comrades stayed behind one by one, and you alone escaped to rejoin Alphinaud and take refuge in Coerthas. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "until you alone emerged from the tunnels beneath [[Ul'dah]] to be reunited with Alphinaud and seek refuge in [[Coerthas]]"
  - **M242a** Count Edmont has made you, Alphinaud and Tataru wards of House Fortemps. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "Count Edmont has decreed that the three of you be taken in as wards of House Fortemps."
  - **M242b** Haurchefant offers the family manor as the Scions' new headquarters. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "Pray consider our manor your new headquarters"
  - **M242g** Haurchefant says any missing allies who are found will be welcome at the manor. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "should any of your missing allies be found─as I am certain they shall─they will of course be welcome to join you there."
  - **M242c** Ishgard is devoted to Halone and ruled by Archbishop Thordan VII of the Ishgardian Orthodox Church. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "A great and proud nation devoted to Halone, the Fury, ruled by Thordan VII, Archbishop of the Ishgardian Orthodox Church..."
  - **M242d** After a thousand years of war, Ishgard had forgotten peace. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "A land that after a thousand years of war had forgotten what it was to be at peace."

</details>

### The Sea of Clouds (`evt-the-sea-of-clouds`, event)

**#245b only · main**

> You, Alphinaud and Tataru are wards of House Fortemps in Ishgard, and Count Edmont has set you to help his sons. His second son, Emmanellain, who longs to escape his brother's shadow, took you to Camp Cloudtop in the Sea of Clouds to aid House Haillenarte. Its commander, Ser Laniaitte, is the elder sister of Francel, whom you once saved, and thinks little of Emmanellain. Her airship, the Protector, is under repair, hampered by clashes with the Vanu Vanu.

Sources shown: Coming to Ishgard — main scenario quest (3.0); The Better Half — main scenario quest (3.0); Onwards and Upwards — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M242a** Count Edmont has made you, Alphinaud and Tataru wards of House Fortemps. *Coming to Ishgard* (3.0, main): "Count Edmont has decreed that the three of you be taken in as wards of House Fortemps."
  - **M244d** Edmont asks you to help his sons, Artoirel and Emmanellain, with their duties. *The Better Half* (3.0, main): "to aid Artoirel and Emmanellain in their duties."
  - **M245ba** Emmanellain, Edmont's second son, longs to escape his elder brother's shadow. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "has long dreamed of emerging from beneath his elder brother's shadow"
  - **M245bc** Emmanellain's mission is to aid House Haillenarte. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "we are to aid the good men and women of House Haillenarte."
  - **M245bd** Camp Cloudtop was built to warn of Dravanian incursions. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "Camp Cloudtop was established to provide early warning of impending Dravanian incursions."
  - **M245be** Ser Laniaitte of House Haillenarte commands Camp Cloudtop. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "I am Ser Laniaitte de Haillenarte, commander of the forces stationed here at Camp Cloudtop."
  - **M245bg** Laniaitte is the elder sister of Francel, whose unjust execution you prevented. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "Lady Laniaitte explains that she is the elder sister of Lord [[Francel]], whose unjust execution you prevented during your search for the ''Enterprise'' long ago."
  - **M245bh** Laniaitte thinks little of Emmanellain, who does not notice. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "though the young lord seems oblivious to her low opinion of him."
  - **M245bf** The camp's great airship, the Protector, is under repair, hampered by skirmishes with the Vanu Vanu. *Onwards and Upwards* (3.0, main): "our efforts have been hampered by an indigenous beast tribe known as the Vanu Vanu, with whom we have had several skirmishes already."

</details>

### Friends in Chains (`evt-friends-in-chains`, event)

**#259 only · main**

> Count Edmont had only begun to thank you for your work at Falcon's Nest and Camp Cloudtop when word came that Ser Grinnaux of the Heavens' Ward, the archbishop's personal guard, had arrested Alphinaud and Tataru for heresy. The lord commander, Ser Aymeric, believed them innocent but could not overrule the Ward, and Edmont suspects a plot by House Dzemael against House Fortemps. You won the trial by combat that the law demanded, and your friends went free.

Sources shown: Divine Intervention — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M259k** Edmont has heard of all you did at Falcon's Nest and Camp Cloudtop. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "Having been informed of all you accomplished during your time in [[Falcon's Nest]] and [[Camp Cloudtop]], Count [[Edmont]] wishes to express his heartfelt gratitude."
  - **M259a** Ser Grinnaux of the Heavens' Ward has arrested Alphinaud and Tataru for fomenting heresy. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "have been arrested by a knight of the [[Heavens' Ward]]—one “[[Ser Grinnaux]]”—on the charge of fomenting heresy."
  - **M259b** The Heavens' Ward is the archbishop's personal guard: twelve knights who answer only to him. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "the personal guard of the [[Thordan VII|archbishop]]. These twelve chosen sers answer to none save the archbishop himself, and their testimony is unimpeachable."
  - **M259g** Aymeric, the lord commander, believes them innocent but cannot overrule the Heavens' Ward. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "Though Ser Aymeric believes your friends to be innocent, he is powerless to intervene as the knight who accused them is a member of the Heavens' Ward"
  - **M259f** Edmont believes the charges are a political ploy against House Fortemps. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "The count believes the charges leveled against your friends to be nothing more than a political ploy to defame [[House Fortemps]]."
  - **M259e** Edmont suspects another member of House Dzemael is manipulating Grinnaux. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "'Tis like that one such member of House Dzemael is manipulating Ser Grinnaux, for he is not a man to dabble in politics of his own volition."
  - **M259c** Only a trial by combat can disprove the charge. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "by granting victory in a trial by combat between the accuser and the accused."
  - **M259i** You defeat Grinnaux and his second in the trial, and your friends go free. *Divine Intervention* (3.0, main): "you defeat Ser Grinnaux and [[Ser Paulecrain]], thus earning your comrades their freedom."

</details>

> As Nidhogg's Dravanian Horde gathers to renew its assault on Ishgard, purple smoke drew Lady Iceheart to you. Iceheart agreed to take you to Hraesvelgr instead. Midgardsormr noted that his mistress's blessing on you has strengthened, and your Crystal of Ice flared.

Sources shown: To Siege or Not to Siege — main scenario quest (3.0); Camp of the Convictors — main scenario quest (3.0); Purple Flame, Purple Flame — main scenario quest (3.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M264a** The Dravanian Horde gathers to renew its assault on Ishgard. *To Siege or Not to Siege* (3.0, main): "It would seem the [[Dravanian Horde|Horde]] gathers once more to renew its assault upon the city."
  - **M269b** Purple smoke in the highlands summons the heretics. *Camp of the Convictors* (3.0, main): "Send up some purple smoke, and the bastards come to you."
  - **M270b** In her tale, the maid Shiva asked the wyrm Hraesvelgr to consume her so their spirits would be joined forever. *Purple Flame, Purple Flame* (3.0, main): "Unable to bear the thought of their separation, the maid bid the wyrm consume her, that their spirits might be entwined for eternity."
  - **M270c** Iceheart says Nidhogg lost an eye to Elezen treachery. *Purple Flame, Purple Flame* (3.0, main): "Nidhogg─he who now stands poised to unleash his wyrmlings upon Ishgard─was the great dragon who lost an eye to Elezen treachery."
  - **M270d** Estinien kept the Eye with him to draw Nidhogg away from Ishgard. *Purple Flame, Purple Flame* (3.0, main): "Indeed, it was for that very reason that I kept it with me as I roamed the land, attempting to draw him away from the city."
  - **M270e** Iceheart agrees to take you to Hraesvelgr. *Purple Flame, Purple Flame* (3.0, main): "You ''still'' believe that a peaceable solution can be found? Very well. I will take you to him."
  - **M270f** Midgardsormr notes that his mistress's blessing on you is stronger than it was. *Purple Flame, Purple Flame* (3.0, main): "Curious... The vestiges of thy mistress's blessing are not as faint as once they were..."
  - **M270g** Your Crystal of Ice flares as you set out for the dragons' homeland. *Purple Flame, Purple Flame* (3.0, main): "As you resolve to depart for the dragons' homeland, the light of your Crystal of Ice suddenly flares once more..."

**#285 only · main**

> On Sohm Al's summit you are seeking Hraesvelgr, the great wyrm who may yet talk Nidhogg out of his war on Ishgard. **#314 only · main**

> Archbishop Thordan fled Ishgard by airship for a place called Azys Lla, and you and Alphinaud are hunting him. After you slew Bismarck, the archbishop took the key to Azys Lla from you. ### Lyse (`char-lyse`, character)

**3.56 only · main** · Also searchable as: Yda

> The Scion you knew as Yda: Yda's younger sister, who served for years in her mask and name. **#397–#405 · main**

> The Ala Mhigan Resistance, allied with the Eorzean Alliance through Conrad in Rhalgr's Reach. Together they destroyed imperial prototype weapons at East End without a single casualty, and its ranks are swelling with recruits and with Scions; once they are trained, Conrad will propose an assault on Castellum Velodyna.

Sources shown: A Bargain Struck — main scenario quest (4.0); Best Served with Cold Steel — main scenario quest (4.0); Let Fill Your Hearts with Pride — main scenario quest (4.0); Where Men Go as One — main scenario quest (4.0)

  - **M397e** Once the recruits are trained, Conrad will propose an assault on Castellum Velodyna. *Where Men Go as One* (4.0, main): "Once our new recruits have received sufficient training, I will propose to General Aldynn that we draw up plans for an assault on Castellum Velodyna."

The Sharlayan scholar who came to help is Krile, Minfilia's dear friend, who knew the twins at the Studium. She hopes to follow the trail Thancred left when Y'shtola sent him away, but needs Matoya's Crystal Eye. Vidofnir seemed open to Ishgard's proposal.

Sources shown: An Uncertain Future — main scenario quest (3.1); Another Time, Another Place — main scenario quest (3.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M336g** The hunt for Minfilia and Thancred is at a standstill. *An Uncertain Future* (3.1, main): "the hunt for [[Minfilia Warde|Minfilia]] and [[Thancred]] remains at a standstill."
  - **M338a** The scholar is Krile, a dear friend of Minfilia. *Another Time, Another Place* (3.1, main): "The scholar is revealed to be none other than [[Krile]], a dear friend of Minfilia."
  - **M338b** Krile knew the twins at the Studium. *Another Time, Another Place* (3.1, main): "you learn that the woman also knew the Leveilleur twins during their time at the [[The Studium|Studium]]."
  - **M338f** Krile hopes to follow a trail Thancred left when Y'shtola sent him away. *Another Time, Another Place* (3.1, main): "Simply put, assuming Thancred left some manner of trail when you whisked him away"
  - **M338c** Krile's plan to find Thancred needs Matoya's Crystal Eye. *Another Time, Another Place* (3.1, main): "she explains that she has a plan to locate Thancred. However, it will require the use of Master [[Matoya]]'s Crystal Eye"
  - **M338d** Vidofnir seemed open to Aymeric's proposal. *Another Time, Another Place* (3.1, main): "She must discuss Ser Aymeric's proposal with Hraesvelgr, of course, but she seemed amenable to the suggestion."

</details>

**#340 only · main**

> Minfilia has been missing since the Scions fled the royal banquet in Ul'dah, but you found Thancred: Y'shtola's forbidden magicks sent him into the wilderness, and he followed the Vath's tales to the Gnath, who had summoned Ravana again. A party of adventurers had already beaten Ravana; their leader named them the Warriors of Darkness, walkers of a different path, and a memory he showed recalled a man in black, perhaps an Ascian.

Sources shown: The Parting Glass — main scenario quest (2.55); A Little Slow, a Little Late — main scenario quest (3.1)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **C17** Minfilia stays behind, saying Hydaelyn speaks to her. *The Parting Glass* (2.55, main): "Hydaelyn... She speaks to me. … I must remain behind...but you cannot stay with me."
  - **M340c** Y'shtola's forbidden magicks sent Thancred into the wilderness. *A Little Slow, a Little Late* (3.1, main): "Had I known you intended to use forbidden magicks to deliver me to some godsforsaken wilderness..."
  - **M340a** The Vath say Thancred went to Loth ast Gnath when he heard the Gnath had summoned their god again. *A Little Slow, a Little Late* (3.1, main): "Gone to Loth ast Gnath. Not long ago. When he heard the Onemind had summoned our god once more."
  - **M340b** The Gnath have summoned Ravana again. *A Little Slow, a Little Late* (3.1, main): "the [[Gnath]] had summoned forth [[Ravana]] from the aether once more"
  - **M340d** A party of adventurers was already beating Ravana when you arrived. *A Little Slow, a Little Late* (3.1, main): "a party of adventurers locked in combat with the Lord of the Hive, and having seized the upper hand no less."
  - **M340e** Their leader names them the Warriors of Darkness, walkers of a different path. *A Little Slow, a Little Late* (3.1, main): "Mark well our faces, Warrior of Light, for we are the Warriors of Darkness. Walkers of a different path."
  - **M340f** Krile saw in the leader's memory a fight with a man in black, perhaps an Ascian. *A Little Slow, a Little Late* (3.1, main): "They were confronting a man in black. An Ascian, I think."

</details>

**#343 only · main**

> Minfilia is still missing. In Ishgard the True Brothers of the Faith seized the Vault and its refugees; you, Aymeric and Artoirel freed all but one, and Vidofnir caught the girl Maelie when a priest threw her from the ledge, then warned Nidhogg and his brood have flown. Count Edmont steps aside for Artoirel, and Y'shtola suspects Thancred has lost his magicks. Urianger met Elidibus and the Warriors' leader, and Yda and Papalymo are with the Ala Mhigan Resistance.

### The Conference at Falcon's Nest (`evt-falcons-nest-conference`, event)

**#346 only · main**

> Ser Aymeric means to make peace with the Dravanians: Vidofnir's rescue of a child gave hope, and he is arranging a peace conference at Falcon's Nest for her to attend, with you there in case Nidhogg, implacably opposed, tries to disrupt it. There Lucia, once a foreign spy who pledged herself to Ishgard, oversees a relief to be unveiled. Alphinaud asks you to keep Minfilia's fate from the others.

Sources shown: This War of Ours — main scenario quest (3.2)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M346b** Vidofnir's rescue of a child gave hope of peace between man and dragon. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "Yet in adversity were we blessed with the promise of peace between man and dragon, through Vidofnir's timely rescue of an innocent child."
  - **M346c** Aymeric is arranging a peace conference at Falcon's Nest, to be attended by Vidofnir. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "he has begun making formal arrangements for a peace conference in [[Falcon's Nest]], to be attended by [[Vidofnir]]"
  - **M346d** Aymeric fears Nidhogg, implacably opposed to peace, may disrupt the conference. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "Given Nidhogg's implacable opposition to the peace, it is possible that he and his followers may attempt to disrupt proceedings"
  - **M346e** Lucia was sent to Ishgard as a foreign spy. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "Dispatched to a foreign nation as a spy, it was her duty to infiltrate [[Ishgard]]ian society for her masters' ends."
  - **M346f** Lucia chose instead to pledge herself to Ishgard's cause and war. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "In the end, however, she chose a different path—to pledge herself to another nation's cause, and to join in their war."
  - **M346g** A relief at Falcon's Nest will be unveiled during the conference. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "It conceals a relief that will be unveiled during the conference."
  - **M346a** Alphinaud will tell Tataru and Urianger of Minfilia's fate, but asks you to tell no one else, least of all F'lhaminn. *This War of Ours* (3.2, main): "Although [[Alphinaud]] intends to inform [[Tataru]] and [[Urianger]] of [[Minfilia Warde|Minfilia's]] fate, he asks that you share with no one else what you have learned—especially [[F'lhaminn]]."

</details>

**#350 only · main**

### Conrad (`char-conrad`, character)

**#382–#383 · main**

> Commander of the Ala Mhigan Resistance in Rhalgr's Reach, who sheltered Lyse and Papalymo at great risk. He says Ilberd led good men and women to the Wall and sacrificed them. He reads the Alliance's offer of aid as a war against the Empire by proxy, and must confer with his officers.

Sources shown: The Promise of a New Beginning — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M382a** Conrad commands the Ala Mhigan Resistance in Rhalgr's Reach. *The Promise of a New Beginning* (4.0, main): "[[Conrad Kemp]], the commander of the [[Ala Mhigan Resistance]] in [[Rhalgr's Reach]]"
  - **M382b** Alphinaud thanks Conrad for sheltering Lyse and Papalymo at great risk. *The Promise of a New Beginning* (4.0, main): "pray allow me to thank you for sheltering Yda—forgive me—Lyse and Papalymo at great risk to yourselves."
  - **M382d** Ilberd led Resistance fighters to the Wall and sacrificed them for his ritual. *The Promise of a New Beginning* (4.0, main): "Followed him all the way to the Wall. Good men and women who never came back. … how the bastard had made sacrifices of them for his twisted ritual"
  - **M382f** Conrad sees the offer as the Alliance fighting the Empire by proxy with the Resistance's weaker forces. *The Promise of a New Beginning* (4.0, main): "The Alliance, hoping to avoid a direct confrontation with the superior forces of the Empire, wishes to engage them by proxy with our vastly inferior ones?"
  - **M382g** Conrad and his officers must confer before they answer. *The Promise of a New Beginning* (4.0, main): "My comrades and I must confer on your proposal."

</details>

### Castrum Oriens (`loc-castrum-oriens`, location)

**#380–#404 · main**

> An imperial castrum by the Wall, at the edge of Gyr Abania, which the Eorzean Alliance occupied after the attack on the Wall and the primal's summoning. From its command center Raubahn holds the Alliance's line, and will not advance into Gyr Abania without the Ala Mhigan Resistance.

  - **M380a** After Ilberd's assault on the Wall and his summoning of the primal now called Shinryu, the Alliance had little choice but to occupy Castrum Oriens. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "[[Ilberd]]'s assault on [[Baelsar's Wall]] and subsequent summoning of the primal now known as “[[Shinryu]]” left the [[Eorzean Alliance]] with little choice but to occupy [[Castrum Oriens]]"

We would have you serve as our emissaries and make contact with the Resistance."

### Envoys to the Resistance (`evt-envoys-to-the-resistance`, event)

**#380 only · main**

> The Alliance has occupied Castrum Oriens beside the Wall, but Raubahn will not march into Gyr Abania without the Ala Mhigan Resistance. He sends the Scions as envoys, with Lyse leading the way given her ties to the Resistance. Yugiri and Gosetsu have gone home to fight for Doma, and Cid's search for Omega and Shinryu has found nothing.

Sources shown: Beyond the Great Wall — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M380a** After Ilberd's assault on the Wall and his summoning of the primal now called Shinryu, the Alliance had little choice but to occupy Castrum Oriens. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "[[Ilberd]]'s assault on [[Baelsar's Wall]] and subsequent summoning of the primal now known as “[[Shinryu]]” left the [[Eorzean Alliance]] with little choice but to occupy [[Castrum Oriens]]"
  - **M380c** Lyse leads the Scions to Ala Mhigo, given her ties to the Resistance. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "with [[Lyse]] to lead the way, given her ties to the Resistance."
  - **M380d** Yugiri and Gosetsu return to Doma to aid their comrades against Garlemald. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "The pair have resolved to return to the nation of [[Doma]], in the Far East, to aid their comrades in the fight against Garlemald."
  - **M380e** Raubahn will not proceed without the Ala Mhigan people's support, and makes the Scions his emissaries to the Resistance. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "As stated in my message, the Alliance will not proceed without the support and cooperation of the Ala Mhigan people. We would have you serve as our emissaries and make contact with the Resistance."
  - **M380f** Cid reports that the search for Omega and Shinryu has found nothing. *Beyond the Great Wall* (4.0, main): "apprises you of the latest developments in the search for [[Omega]] and Shinryu: namely, that there have not been any, the fate and whereabouts of both remaining unknown."

</details>

Sources shown: Under the Sea — main scenario quest (4.0); The Whims of the Divine — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M425a** The Kojin mercenaries who serve the Empire are of the Red. *Under the Sea* (4.0, main): "The mercenaries who serve the Empire belong to the Red."
  - **M430b** Bunchin's ceremonial knife opens the Kojin vault on the Isle of Zekki. *The Whims of the Divine* (4.0, main): "Before this blade, that which is sealed shall open. The treasure vault of the Kojin, on the Isle of Zekki."
  - **M430c** An attack on the vault would summon Kojin from all around to defend it. *The Whims of the Divine* (4.0, main): "Were the vault to be attacked, their response would by necessity be immediate. Kojin would be summoned from malms around to defend their treasures."
  - **M430d** Without the Kojin, the imperials lack the troops to hold Isari. *The Whims of the Divine* (4.0, main): "Without the Kojin, the imperials don't have nearly enough troops in Isari to hold off the pirates."

</details>

**#431 only · main**

> Kojin mercenaries who serve the Empire. In their vault on the Isle of Zekki, the treasures they have guarded for generations woke as the great kami Susano, whom their commander hailed.

Sources shown: Under the Sea — main scenario quest (4.0); Breaking and Delivering — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M425a** The Kojin mercenaries who serve the Empire are of the Red. *Under the Sea* (4.0, main): "The mercenaries who serve the Empire belong to the Red."

  - **M431d** The Red have guarded the kami's blade and glass for generations. *Breaking and Delivering* (4.0, main): "We who have guarded your blade and glass for generations─your faithful Kojin!"

**#432–#433 · main**

> Kojin mercenaries of the Empire, who abandoned their posts at Isari to defend the Isle of Zekki. Their great kami, Susano, has been slain.

### A Bargain with the Confederacy (`evt-a-bargain-with-the-confederacy`, event)

**#419 only · main**

> Soroban, a Blue Kojin, carried you to Othard's coast. In Isari, occupied by imperial forces, the viceroy Yotsuyu forced one villager to execute another, and Gosetsu, who calls her a traitor to her homeland, surrendered to her so you could plan his rescue. On his advice, Alisaie and Lyse led you to Onokoro, a large settlement held by the Confederacy.

Sources shown: To Bend with the Wind — main scenario quest (4.0)

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  - **M419a** Soroban, relieved that you will not judge his Blue Kojin for the deeds of the Red, carries you on to Othard. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "Relieved that you will not judge him and his fellow Blue Kojin harshly for the deeds of the Red, Soroban is eager to take you the rest of the way to Othard"
  - **M419b** Isari, a village on Othard's coast, is occupied by imperial forces. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "turn your attentions to Isari, which you soon discover to be occupied by imperial forces"

  - **M419d** Yotsuyu forces one villager to execute another, then has him shot for refusing to kill his own parents. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "Yotsuyu forces one villager to execute another, before having him shot for refusing to kill his own parents."
  - **M419g** Gosetsu calls Yotsuyu the traitor who sold her homelands to the Garleans. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "The traitor who sold her homelands to the Garleans—Yotsuyu!"
  - **M419e** Gosetsu surrenders himself to the viceroy, expecting her to question him and give you time to plan a rescue. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "Gosetsu resolves to end the madness by surrendering himself into the viceroy's custody, reasoning that she will wish to question him thoroughly, giving you time to formulate a rescue plan"
  - **M419h** The large settlement on Onokoro, with its own aetheryte, is under the Confederacy's control. *To Bend with the Wind* (4.0, main): "It would seem that Gosetsu intended for you to seek the aid of the Confederacy, as the large settlement─complete with its own aetheryte─appears to be under their control."

### The Kojin Treasures (`evt-the-kojin-treasures`, event)

**#429 only · main**

> To win the Confederacy's help in freeing Isari, you wagered to deprive the Empire of its Red Kojin allies. Searching for the sacred jewel the Blue Kojin seek, you met Yugiri's parents in Sui-no-Sato, who have had no word of her since she fought in Doma's rebellion. Their lamps led you to the Yasakani-no-Magatama in a sunken ship.

**#430 only · main**

> You found the Yasakani-no-Magatama, a sacred Kojin jewel, while seeking a way to draw the Red Kojin away from the imperial garrison in Isari. Bunchin gave you a knife to open the Kojin vault on the Isle of Zekki, which holds the jewel's two siblings: an attack there would pull the Red from their posts. Soroban will ready the Confederacy to strike.

Sources shown: In Darkness the Magatama Dreams — main scenario quest (4.0); The Whims of the Divine — main scenario quest (4.0)
